headline: No live signal. Ledger unchanged at 24 trades, -2.7 bps/trade (-64.4 total). Sample still too thin to judge.
regime_note: BTC ~$78.7k, well above the $63-66k band where most ledger trades were struck; the biggest wins came from fading the late-August spike into the mid-to-high $70ks. No new fills since last update, so nothing material has changed.
assessment_md:
**What's happening:** No trade signal right now (`signal: 0`), and the ledger is unchanged from last time — still 24 resolved trades. So there is genuinely nothing new to react to.

**The numbers:** Over all 24 trades, the strategy has won 37.5% and averaged **-2.7 bps per trade** (-64.4 bps cumulative) after a 3 bps cost assumption. That looks bad on its face, but recall the whole edge was only ~4 bps gross with a ~3.9 bps breakeven — this was always a marginal, likely-not-net-profitable candidate. The recent 5-trade window is slightly positive (+0.6 bps net, 60% win), driven by a cluster of good short fills into the Aug 21-23 rally (e.g. +48.7 and +16.2 bps). A couple of large losers earlier (-60.9, -28.1 bps) dominate the total.

**What this does and doesn't tell us:** 24 trades is far too few to conclude anything. At ~4 bps expected edge with double-digit-bps single-trade swings, the noise dwarfs the signal — a handful of trades can flip the running total either way. The -2.7 bps mean is consistent with both 'no real edge' and 'small edge plus bad luck.'

**Bottom line:** No degradation alert warranted, but no encouragement either. Separately, `edge_search_survivors: 0` — nothing clears the stricter 5 bps two-venue bar. Treat this as a research artifact, not a profitable strategy. Keep watching; don't act on these numbers.
